simple.meaning: יָאַל (yâʼal) is a Hebrew word meaning “properly, to be slack , i.e. (figuratively) to be foolish.” BibleIQ connects the English word back to this source word so its use can be compared across Scripture.
simple.biblicalBackground: יָאַל (H2973) appears 4 times in the Hebrew Bible, beginning at Numbers 12:11, with occurrences in Numbers, Isaiah, Jeremiah.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to יָאַל (H2973) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: English translations can use the same English word for different Hebrew words. BibleIQ anchors the study in יָאַל (H2973) before moving outward to related references.
simple.summary: יָאַל (yâʼal) / H2973 is traced through Numbers 12:11, Isaiah 19:13, Jeremiah 5:4, Jeremiah 50:36 using source-language evidence and occurrence comparison.

definitions.short: properly, to be slack , i.e. (figuratively) to be foolish
definitions.full: H2973. yaal I. [ יָאַל ] verb be foolish (compare I. אול ) — Niph`al Perfect 3masculine plural נוֺאֲלוּ Isa 19:3 ; Jer 5:4 ; וְנֹאָ֑לוּ 50:36 ; 1 plural נוֺאַלְנוּ Num 12:11 ; — do or act foolishly: — 1 shew wicked folly = sin חָטָאנוּ וַאֲשֶׁר נוֺאַלְנוּ אֲשֶׁר חַטָּאת Num 12:11 (J); in Jer 5:4 an exhibition of this folly is ascribed to ignorance. 2 become fools , lacking insight and judgment: צֹעַן שְׂרֵי נוֺאֲלוּ Isa 19:13 the princes of Zoan have become fools (|| נֹף שָׂרֵי נִשְּׁאוּ , and, in 19:11 צֹעַן שָׂרֵי אֱוִילִים , etc.); וְנֹאָ֑לוּ אֶלהַֿבַּדִּים חֶדֶב Jer 50:36 a sword is against the praters, and they shall become fools — be shewn up as such (|| ׃ חָֽתּוּ ).
